subject: music
topicDisplay: Area Of Study 6 Innovations In Music 1900 To Present
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A passing note is which type of non-chord tone?
options: Approached and left by step in the same direction filling a melodic gap
A note that returns to its starting pitch
A sustained dissonance held over a barline
Approached by leap and left by step
questions.explain: A passing note connects two chord tones a third apart, approached and quitted by step in the same direction.

questions.q: In Indian classical music the term 'bol' refers to...?
options: Mnemonic syllables used to represent and recite drum strokes or rhythms
questions.explain: Bols are spoken mnemonic syllables representing tabla strokes and rhythmic patterns.

questions.q: A modulation from C major to G major is a move to which related key?
questions.explain: G major is the dominant key of C major, a closely related key with one extra sharp.

questions.q: A perfect cadence is formed by which progression?
questions.explain: A perfect (authentic) cadence moves from the dominant (V) to the tonic (I).

questions.q: In a major key, which chord built on the dominant typically functions as the dominant seventh?
options: A major seventh chord on the tonic
A major-minor (dominant) seventh chord on scale degree 5
A minor seventh chord on the supertonic
A diminished seventh chord on the leading note
questions.explain: The dominant seventh is a major-minor seventh chord built on the fifth degree, comprising a major triad plus a minor seventh.

questions.q: A German augmented sixth chord contains which intervals above the bass?
options: Major third, augmented fourth and augmented sixth
Major third and augmented sixth only
Major third, perfect fifth and augmented sixth
questions.explain: The German sixth comprises a major third, perfect fifth and augmented sixth above the bass note.

questions.q: An interrupted cadence most commonly progresses from which chord to which?
questions.explain: An interrupted (deceptive) cadence moves from V to vi, thwarting the expected resolution to the tonic.

questions.q: A diminished seventh chord is built from which stacked intervals?
options: A major third and two minor thirds
questions.explain: The diminished seventh chord consists of three stacked minor thirds, dividing the octave symmetrically.

questions.q: The 'tabla' is...?
options: A pair of hand drums of different sizes and pitches
questions.explain: The tabla is a pair of tuned hand drums central to North Indian rhythmic accompaniment.

questions.q: A melodic sequence is best described as which?
options: The simultaneous sounding of two melodies
A note held against changing harmony
The inversion of a melodic line
The repetition of a melodic pattern at a different pitch level
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic (or harmonic) idea successively higher or lower in pitch.

questions.q: In the context of performance, 'idiomatic writing' for an instrument means...?
options: Writing that ignores the instrument's natural strengths
Writing only in the treble clef
Writing that suits the technique, range and characteristic capabilities of the instrument
questions.explain: Idiomatic writing exploits the natural technique, range and strengths of the specific instrument.

questions.q: In fusion music, an artist such as Ravi Shankar collaborating with Western musicians most exemplifies...?
options: The blending of Indian classical techniques (raga, tala, sitar) with Western elements
questions.explain: Such collaborations blend Indian classical features like raga, tala and sitar with Western musical elements.

questions.q: In figured bass, the symbol '6' beneath a bass note indicates which chord position?
questions.explain: A bare '6' indicates a first-inversion triad, with the bass note a sixth and a third above it.

questions.q: 'Call and response' is a texture common in African (and African-American) music in which...?
options: A leader's phrase (call) is answered by a group (response)
The music has no fixed pulse
Two unrelated melodies are played simultaneously
All voices sing exactly the same line throughout
questions.explain: In call and response a soloist's call is answered by the group's response, an antiphonal texture.

questions.q: A 'reel', another Celtic dance type, is usually in...?
options: Simple quadruple time (4/4 or cut common) with a flowing quaver movement
questions.explain: The reel is a fast dance in simple quadruple time with continuous even quavers.

questions.q: The relative minor of G major is which key?
questions.explain: The relative minor shares the key signature of G major (one sharp) and is E minor.

questions.q: A homophonic texture is characterised by which?
options: A melody supported by chordal accompaniment
Two or more independent equal melodic lines
questions.explain: Homophony features a principal melody accompanied by chords, all parts moving largely together.

questions.q: In an Indian classical ensemble, which pairing of instruments is most typical?
questions.explain: The sitar plays the melody while the tabla provides the rhythmic accompaniment.

questions.q: Gamelan ensembles commonly use which two tuning systems?
questions.explain: Gamelan typically uses the five-note slendro and the seven-note pelog tuning systems.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, a 'raga' is best defined as...?
options: A fixed rhythmic cycle of beats
A melodic framework of notes and characteristic phrases used as the basis for improvisation
The drone instrument that sustains the tonic
questions.explain: A raga is the melodic framework, comprising a set of notes and characteristic phrases, on which improvisation is built.

questions.q: The continuous sustained background pitch in Indian classical music, often provided by the tanpura, is called the...?
questions.explain: The drone is the sustained pitch (usually tonic and dominant) supplied by the tanpura beneath the melody.

questions.q: A 4-3 suspension resolves by which means?
options: The fourth leaps up to the sixth
The fourth steps down to the third
The third rises to the fourth
questions.explain: In a 4-3 suspension the dissonant fourth resolves downwards by step onto the consonant third.

questions.q: A plagal cadence consists of which progression?
questions.explain: The plagal ('Amen') cadence moves from the subdominant (IV) to the tonic (I).

questions.q: The Latin American 'clave' is best described as...?
options: A characteristic two-bar rhythmic pattern underpinning many Afro-Cuban styles
questions.explain: The clave is a foundational two-bar rhythmic pattern that organises much Afro-Cuban and Latin music.

questions.q: The 'jhalla', the closing section of a North Indian raga performance, is characterised by...?
options: Silence with only the drone sounding
A return to the opening alap
A fast, exciting climax with rapid rhythmic strumming
A slow, free and unmetred mood
questions.explain: The jhalla is the fast, rhythmically exciting climax that ends the performance.

questions.q: In African music, the 'master drummer' typically...?
options: Sets up the instruments before the performance
Leads the ensemble, signalling changes and improvising over the cyclic patterns
questions.explain: The master drummer leads, cues changes and improvises over the underlying cyclic patterns.

questions.q: A 'cyclic' or 'ostinato' pattern, common in African drumming, is...?
options: A pattern that constantly changes and never repeats
A short rhythmic or melodic pattern repeated continuously as a foundation
questions.explain: Cyclic patterns repeat a short rhythmic or melodic cell continuously, forming the music's foundation.

questions.q: In figured bass, the symbols '6/4' indicate which inversion of a triad?
questions.explain: A 6/4 figure denotes a second-inversion triad, with the fifth in the bass.

questions.q: A Picardy third refers to which feature?
options: A chord built on the third degree
A third added above the melody
A minor-key piece ending on a major (raised third) tonic chord
A major piece ending on the minor third
questions.explain: A tierce de Picardie raises the third of the final tonic chord so a minor-key work ends on a major chord.

questions.q: In composition, developing a musical idea through 'sequence' means...?
options: Repeating a melodic pattern at a higher or lower pitch
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic or harmonic pattern at a different pitch level.
